[2111.09708] A Trainable Spectral-Spatial Sparse Coding Model for Hyperspectral Image Restoration Skip to main content Search Submit Donate Log in Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search Electrical Engineering and Systems Science > Image and Video Processing arXiv:2111.09708 (eess) [Submitted on 18 Nov 2021] Title: A Trainable Spectral-Spatial Sparse Coding Model for Hyperspectral Image Restoration Authors: Théo Bodrito (Thoth, Inria, UGA, CNRS, Grenoble INP, LJK), Alexandre Zouaoui (Thoth, Inria, UGA, CNRS, Grenoble INP, LJK), Jocelyn Chanussot (Thoth, Inria, UGA, CNRS, Grenoble INP, LJK), Julien Mairal (Thoth, Inria, UGA, CNRS, Grenoble INP, LJK) View a PDF of the paper titled A Trainable Spectral-Spatial Sparse Coding Model for Hyperspectral Image Restoration, by Th\'eo Bodrito (Thoth and 23 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Hyperspectral imaging offers new perspectives for diverse applications, ranging from the monitoring of the environment using airborne or satellite remote sensing, precision farming, food safety, planetary exploration, or astrophysics. Unfortunately, the spectral diversity of information comes at the expense of various sources of degradation,  and the lack of accurate ground-truth "clean" hyperspectral signals acquired on the spot makes restoration tasks challenging. In particular, training deep neural networks for restoration is difficult, in contrast to traditional RGB imaging problems where deep models tend to shine. In this paper, we advocate instead for a hybrid approach based on sparse coding principles that retains the interpretability of classical techniques encoding domain knowledge with handcrafted image priors, while allowing to train model parameters end-to-end without massive amounts of data. We show on various denoising benchmarks that our method is computationally efficient and  significantly outperforms the state of the art.
